summary: Compare two lines of sight from opposite orbital positions and keep the half-angle convention explicit.
objective: Build a stellar parallax diagram with opposite Earth positions, a nearby star and a distant reference backdrop.
intent_signals: Build a stellar parallax diagram with opposite Earth positions, a nearby star and a distant reference backdrop.
Compare two lines of sight from opposite orbital positions and keep the half-angle convention explicit.
example_prompts: Build a stellar parallax diagram with opposite Earth positions, a nearby star and a distant reference backdrop.
Create an explorable 3D explanation of stellar parallax with angle inset.
negative_signals: No proper motion, aberration, measurement noise or Bayesian distance inference from uncertain parallaxes.
not_for: No proper motion, aberration, measurement noise or Bayesian distance inference from uncertain parallaxes.

entities.name: Observation baseline
entities.guidance: Place two observer markers at -b and +b around a central Sun marker; label baseline 2*b and its half b separately.

entities.name: Nearby star and backdrop
entities.guidance: Show one selected nearby star and a distant fixed direction grid; mark that background stars are treated as effectively fixed for this ideal experiment.

entities.name: Angle inset
entities.guidance: Draw a magnified parallax angle inset tied to the same numeric calculation, distinguishing p from the full apparent displacement 2*p.

state_contract.model: Ideal right-triangle geometry: star on a line perpendicular to the midpoint of a baseline of length 2*b, b>0; parallax half-angle p=atan(b/d), d>0. Full angular separation of the symmetric sightlines is 2*p.
state_contract.authority: Baseline endpoints and star distance own sightline directions and measured angle; screen exaggeration never substitutes for the model angle.
actions: Move the nearby star farther along the perpendicular line.
Switch between the two observer views.

invariants: At fixed baseline, increasing distance decreases parallax angle.
The full symmetric sightline separation is twice the defined parallax half-angle.
Geometry uses d=b/tan(p); the small-angle d≈b/p relation requires p in radians and a stated approximation.
motion_guidance: Animate camera transfer only between declared observation positions; do not move the star to fake apparent displacement.
Show observation epoch labels as schematic positions, not dates of actual stellar measurements.
known_limits: No proper motion, aberration, measurement noise or Bayesian distance inference from uncertain parallaxes.
Real stellar angles are tiny; geometric distance and visual angular exaggeration must remain separate.
Curated recipe only; no runtime scene or rendered behavior has been verified for this record.

claims.statement: Stellar parallax uses apparent positional displacement from different observing positions and a known baseline to infer distance by trigonometry.
claims.scope: Ideal geometric construction; the symmetric baseline and perpendicular star direction are chosen for clarity.

source_refs.locator: Parallax angle, Earth-Sun baseline and trigonometric distance

object_craft.structure: Place two observer markers at -b and +b around a central Sun marker; label baseline 2*b and its half b separately.
object_craft.material: Small luminous star markers are visual symbols with disclosed sizing; opaque sightlines and an angle inset carry the measurements.
